newsitem.title: UK: Euro bancassurance pressure life companies -report.
newsitem.headline: Euro bancassurance pressure life companies -report.

text.p: The rapidly growing 'bancassurance' sector is squeezing the profit margins of traditional life insurance companies, management consultancy Datamonitor said in a report on Monday.
Many bancassurers gain their competitive edge in life insurance from tax advantages, the brand name of their parent bank, distribution networks and customer databases, Datamonitor said.
"Although traditional insurers are catching up in terms of marketing, they are struggling to distribute their insurance as cheaply and as effectively," it added.
Bancassurers are usually owned by, or closely linked to, a bank and most concentrate on the sale of life insurance and pensions.
They now account for 19.2 percent of the European life and pensions market, according to the Datamonitor report 'Bancassurance in Europe.'
French companies accounted for $36.9 billion of Europe's bancassurance premium income in 1995, followed by Britain in second place with $6.3 billion and Spain with $5.4 billion.

Many European bancassurers achieved high growth rates in recent years, although UK companies tended to lag their counterparts elsewhere. Fifty-nine percent of bancassurers achieved average annual growth rates of over 25 percent between 1992 and 1995.

The top 10 by premium income in Europe in 1995 were French companies Predicia, Ecureuil Vie, Natio Vie, Sogecap & Sogenal, ACM, UAF, Fructivie, Socapi, Dutch company Interpolis and the UK's NatWest Life.
